title: 2D U-Net Framework for Multiclass Automated Segmentation of Healthy Structures, Ischemic Stroke, and Glioblastoma in the Rat Brain

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《2D U-Net Framework for Multiclass Automated Segmentation of Healthy Structures, Ischemic Stroke, and Glioblastoma in the Rat Brain》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · nbm70432-sec-0001-p1】Rodents are widely employed in preclinical research to investigate a range of brain diseases, including stroke, and brain tumors, offering invaluable models for exploring the underlying mechanisms of neurological conditions. In these studies, in vivo imaging technologies, particularly magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), play a vital role in monitoring disease progression, evaluating treatment effects, and gaining insights into the evolving dynamics of neural changes over time [1, 2, 3].

【Introduction · nbm70432-sec-0001-p5】To overcome these collective limitations, our goal is to develop advanced tools that surpass the performance of existing methods while introducing new resources and contributing valuable datasets to the scientific community. Here, we present and validate three 2D U‐Net‐based pipelines enable automatic segmentation and volume quantification using MRI datasets for: (i) multiple ROIs, including the striatum, neocortex, hippocampus, and whole brain from T2‐weighted imaging (T2‐wi) in healthy subjects; (ii) ischemic stroke lesion volumes and the lesion‐bearing brain using T2‐relaxation maps from a transient ischemic stroke model; and (iii) brain tumor lesions using T2‐wi from a glioblastoma rat model. We employed four metrics to evaluate the segmentation performance of the proposed frameworks. Additionally, we compared our tools with existing methods to validate their state‐of‐the‐art performance and assess their suitability for preclinical and translational research. By enhancing the accuracy, efficiency, and applicability of brain segmentation or lesion analysis, we aim to provide more reliable and comprehensive resources for preclinical research, ultimately improving the study of neurological diseases and their treatments.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《2D U-Net Framework for Multiclass Automated Segmentation of Healthy Structures, Ischemic Stroke, and Glioblastoma in the Rat Brain》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Implementation · nbm70432-sec-0013-p1】The analysis was developed using a Python script, and the datasets are available for download at https://github.com/NOBEL‐MRI/Rat‐Datasets. Across the three experimental cohorts, a total of 111 animals were evaluated, yielding 1949 original 2D MRI slices. Following the threefold data augmentation expansion, the definitive volumetric matrix comprised 5847 images. To prevent data leakage between the training and test sets, splitting was performed at the animal level, that is, all (augmented) slices originating from a given animal were assigned exclusively to either the training or the test subset—rather than at the level of individual slices, as follows: (i) Cohort 1 (anatomical target): comprising 28 healthy subjects (392 baseline slices before augmentation), the dataset was split into 22 animals / 308 slices for network training and six animals /84 slices for independent testing. (ii) Cohort 2 (ischemic stroke): comprising 33 subjects monitored across longitudinal phases, 11 animals at 24 h, 10 animals at 7 d, and 12 animals at 14 d after stroke (462 baseline slices before augmentation), the dataset was split into 26 animals/364 slices for training and seven animals /98 slices for independent testing. (iii) Cohort 3 (glioblastoma): comprising 50 subjects evaluated at progressive oncological stage: 24 animals at 7 days, 17 animals at 14 days, and nine animals at 21 days after induction (1095 raw slices before augmentation). The dataset was likewise split at the animal level, with 33 animals reserved for independent testing, with 163 total across different timepoints. Slice counts reported above are prior to the threefold augmentation, which was applied only to the training subset after splitting.

【Quantitative Volumetric Correlation and Methodological Benchmarking · nbm70432-sec-0017-p1】A significant monotonic relationship was observed between the manually annotated ground truth volumes and the automated 2D U‐Net predictions across all experimental conditions (Figure 4a–c). For Cohort 1, the Spearman rank correlation coefficients achieved near‐perfect alignment, yielding ρ=0.99 for the striatum, ρ=0.98 for the neocortex, ρ=0.99 for the hippocampus, and ρ=0.97 for the whole brain. For Cohort 2 (ischemic stroke), robust correlations were obtained for both macro‐structural and physiological parameters, with ρ=0.91 for whole‐brain volume, ρ=0.98 for ischemic lesion volume and ρ=0.82 for localized quantitative T2‐relaxation times. Finally, Cohort 3 (glioblastoma) maintained an excellent correlation of ρ=0.92. Across all cohorts and structural classes, these correlations proved to be extremely robust and statistically definitive (p<10−60), confirming that the automated framework accurately and reliably replicates expert manual volumetric estimations.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《2D U-Net Framework for Multiclass Automated Segmentation of Healthy Structures, Ischemic Stroke, and Glioblastoma in the Rat Brain》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Model Training and Validation: Loss Functions, Batch Size, and Number of Epoch · nbm70432-sec-0010-p5】For Cohort 1, categorical cross entropy was employed, as it is commonly used in multiclass segmentation (Equation (4)). This loss function predicts a probability for each class present in the true label. For Cohort 2, the Tversky Index with α = 0.7 (minimized as Tversky Loss = 1 − Tversky Index) was used (Equation (5)). This function introduces two hyperparameters that control the weight of false positive‐ (FP) and false‐negative (FN) errors, effectively addressing class imbalance [45]. Tversky Loss was chosen over Dice Loss for stroke segmentation due to its ability to better manage class imbalance and small lesion size by weighting false negatives more heavily, thereby improving sensitivity and reducing undersegmentation. In Cohort 3, binary cross entropy was applied (Equation (6)), which measures the difference between the predicted probabilities and the actual binary labels (0 or 1).

【Model Training and Validation: Loss Functions, Batch Size, and Number of Epoch · nbm70432-sec-0010-p7】where TP stands for true positives, and α is a hyperparameter that adjusts the weight of FNs (the higher the α the more the FNs are penalized). Formally, β = 1 − α weights false negatives; with α = 0.7 (β = 0.3), false negatives are penalized more heavily than false positives, favoring sensitivity and reducing undersegmentation of the lesion, consistent with the values reported in Results.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《2D U-Net Framework for Multiclass Automated Segmentation of Healthy Structures, Ischemic Stroke, and Glioblastoma in the Rat Brain》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · nbm70432-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Schematic workflow and the proposed 2D U‐Net architecture. The overall pipeline encompasses: (a) raw MRI data acquisition, (b) manual expert annotation (ground truth) and image preprocessing, (c) data augmentation and model training, and (d) performance validation. (e) The 2D U‐Net architecture comprises a contracting encoder path to capture contextual features and a symmetrical expanding decoder path for precise spatial localization. The network accommodates distinct MRI modalities as inputs (T2‐wi or T2‐relaxation maps) to generate the corresponding multiclass structural or pathological segmentation masks as outputs.

【FIGURE 2 · nbm70432-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Qualitative segmentation performance across the three experimental cohorts. From left to right, each panel showcases: the raw input MRI slice, the corresponding preprocessed and normalized image tensor, and a direct spatial overlay comparing the manual expert annotation (ground truth, highlighted in green/solid boundaries) against the 2D U‐Net predicted mask (highlighted in red/dashed boundaries). Row 1 (Cohort 1) displays the multiclass delineation of healthy anatomical regions (striatum, neocortex, and hippocampus); Row 2 (Cohort 2) illustrates the segmentation of the ischemic stroke lesion and the surrounding brain parenchyma; Row 3 (Cohort 3) depicts the boundary tracking of the glioblastoma tumor mass.

【FIGURE 3 · nbm70432-fig-0003】FIGURE 3 Volumetric 3D surface rendering of the structural MRI scans and automated segmentations. Spatial continuity and geometric accuracy are visualized via 3D multiplanar reconstructions for each experimental target. The semitransparent surface models of the original T2‐wi and T2‐relaxation scans are overlaid with the integrated 2D U‐Net predicted masks, demonstrating the robust slice‐to‐slice volumetric consistency of the framework across healthy brain structures, ischemic infarct volumes, and infiltrative glioblastoma boundaries.
